request.questionText: Which of the following statements is true of "colliders" in the context of regression modeling? Select all correct answers.

choices.label: A
choices.text: "Collider" is just another synonym for a confounder.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Confounders tend to be causally "upstream" of X and Y, while colliders are causally "downstream" of X and Y.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Exploratory data analysis (like plots and simple model fits) will help you tell the difference between a confounder and a collider.

choices.label: D
choices.text: If our goal is to isolate a partial relationship between X and Y, confounders and colliders must both be included in our regression model.

choices.label: E
choices.text: If our goal is to isolate a partial relationship between X and Y, confounders should be included in the model, while colliders should be excluded.
